items: Badges. The README and the console show two more badges: format Agent Skills and last commit.

Starting guides for the genres that had none, mechanic recipes and design rules. New genre skills with a reference pack each (79 items in all, in the kit's own words and written for UEFN): Strategy (tower and wave defense), Shooter, Deathrun & Platformer, Adventure & RPG (quests and escape rooms), Simulation & Tycoon, plus a reference pack for Survival and one for Roguelike. They reach the Skills page as one proposal per genre and nothing applies until the owner approves; learned lessons always outrank them. Seven new recipes in the `mechanics` skill: weighted loot box, wave director, currency and shop, persistent levels, hunger and needs, ordered objectives, course checkpoints (the six with Verse are compile-checked in the editor before they count as built). Four short discipline skills (`game-feel-uefn`, `level-design-uefn`, `camera-audio-uefn`, `game-ai-uefn`) and an index (`uefn-disciplines`) that says which one to read for a concept. `validate_skills.py` now checks discipline skills (trigger words in the description, a "When not to use" line, a size limit, existing skill names), and the token baseline for skill entry points rose by 16 000 characters for these.

The Motion button works again on every page. Six reduced-motion rules (Docs: the step arrows and rings, the live bars; Console: the hub, the alert, the thinking dots; Flow) still switched the movement off when Windows has animation effects off, even with Motion on. They now carry `html:not(.motion-full)`, and `ui_lint.py` fails the build when a reduced-motion rule lacks it.
release.title: v1.115.0 — Starting guides for five genres, mechanic recipes, design rules, Motion fixed
